title: Psalms Bible Quiz - Chapter 128
description: Ten questions on Psalms 128: the blessings of everyone who fears Yahweh - eating the labor of his hands, a fruitful wife, children like olive plants and peace on Israel.

questions.text: Verse 1 calls blessed everyone who fears Yahweh and who does what?
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:1 says "Blessed is everyone who fears Yahweh, who walks in his ways."

questions.text: What will you eat, according to verse 2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:2 says "For you will eat the labor of your hands."
Psalms 128:2 says "You will be happy, and it will be well with you."

answers.text: You will be happy, and it will be well with you
You will be rich and famous in all the land of Israel
You will rule over many people
You will never grow old or weak

questions.text: What will your wife be like, according to verse 3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:3 says "Your wife will be as a fruitful vine."

answers.text: A palm tree by the water

questions.text: Where in the house will the wife be as a fruitful vine?
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:3 says she will be as a fruitful vine "in the innermost parts of your house."

answers.text: In the innermost parts of your house
At the door of your house
On the roof of your house
In the outer courtyard of your house

questions.text: What will your children be like around your table?
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:3 says "your children like olive plants around your table."

questions.text: Out of where does verse 5 ask Yahweh to bless you?
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:5 says "May Yahweh bless you out of Zion."

questions.text: What may you see all the days of your life, according to verse 5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:5 says "may you see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life."

questions.text: Whom does verse 6 wish that you may see?
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:6 says "Yes, may you see your children's children."

answers.text: The kings of the nations of the earth

questions.text: With which words does the psalm end?
questions.explanation: Psalms 128:6 ends with "Peace be upon Israel."
